To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

emotion regulation therapy (ERT) is a novel treatment for generalized anxiety disorder (GADS) that targets the functional nature of negative self-referent processing (NSRP) by targeting motivational and behavioral consequences of NSRP, and that ERT is superior to an attention control treatment in reducing symptoms of GAD, co-occurring major depressive disorder, worry, and rumination and that these improvements were maintained for nine month following the end of treatment.
Emotion Regulation Therapy, a treatment for Generalized Anxiety and Major Depressive Disorder, was superior to the modified control condition on all clinical outcomes.
Emotion Regulation Therapy is an efficacious treatment for Generalized Anxiety and Major Depressive Disorder, and is superior to a modified attention control treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of emotion regulation in the development and maintenance of psychopathology and the development and evaluation of emotion regulation treatments for anxiety disorders.
understanding the role of emotion regulation in the development and maintenance of psychopathology and the mechanisms underlying its treatment.
the identification, modification, and prevention of the functional nature of worry and rumination, which are the primary targets of our interventions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ERT is an effective treatment for GAD with and without comorbid MDE.
the study provides encouraging support for the use of ERT in the treatment of GAD with co-morbid MDD.
ERT is a promising treatment for GAD and GAD+MDD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ERT is an efficacious treatment for GAD and MDS that is superior to an attention control condition and that this superiority is mediated by changes in emotion regulation.

ERT, which targets the core features of worry and rumination, can be an important tool in treating patients with GAD, and even those with comorbid depression, with a focus on the underlying mechanisms of emotion regulation.
ERT is a novel treatment that targets NSRP, which may be a core mechanism underlying GAD and M.D.D. and may be an important target for improving the treatment response of both disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the integration of principles from affect science and cognitive–behavioral treatment approaches can be used to improve treatment response for patients with complex clinical presentations such as GAD and MDE.

it is possible to develop treatments that target the mechanisms that are associated with the development and maintenance of complex clinical conditions and that these treatments can be delivered in a relatively brief time period.
the integration of affect science with CBT may be particularly helpful for patients with complex clinical conditions.
